## File: Explore.Blazor.Client/Components/Admin/Organization/OrganizationMembersSection.razor
````razor
  1: @* ABOUTME: Displays a summary list of organization members with name, role, and position. *@
  2: @* ABOUTME: Part of the Organization Admin Settings sidebar layout, with a link to the full members management page. *@
  3: 
  4: @using MudBlazor
  5: @using Explore.Blazor.Client.Services
  6: @using Explore.Blazor.Client.Helpers
  7: @inject IOrganizationMemberService MemberService
  8: @inject NavigationManager Navigation
  9: 
 10: <div class="settings-section">
 11:     <div class="settings-section-header">
 12:         <MudText Typo="Typo.h5" Style="font-weight: 700;">Members</MudText>
 13:         <MudText Typo="Typo.body2" Color="Color.Secondary" Class="mt-1">
 14:             People who belong to this organization.
 15:         </MudText>
 16:     </div>
 17: 
 18:     @if (_loading)
 19:     {
 20:         <MudProgressCircular Color="Color.Primary" Indeterminate="true" Size="Size.Small" />
 21:     }
 22:     else if (!_members.Any())
 23:     {
 24:         <MudAlert Severity="Severity.Info" Variant="Variant.Outlined" Dense="true">
 25:             No members found for this organization.
 26:         </MudAlert>
 27:     }
 28:     else
 29:     {
 30:         <MudStack Spacing="2">
 31:             <MudPaper Elevation="0" Class="pa-0 border-solid border-1 mud-border-lines-default rounded-lg overflow-hidden">
 32:                 <MudList T="OrganizationMemberDto" Dense="true" DisablePadding="true">
 33:                     @foreach (var member in _members.Take(MaxPreviewCount))
 34:                     {
 35:                         <MudListItem>
 36:                             <div class="d-flex align-center justify-space-between w-100">
 37:                                 <div class="d-flex align-center gap-3">
 38:                                     <MudAvatar Color="Color.Primary" Size="Size.Small" Variant="Variant.Outlined">
 39:                                         @GetInitial(member)
 40:                                     </MudAvatar>
 41:                                     <div>
 42:                                         <MudText Typo="Typo.body2" Style="font-weight: 600;">
 43:                                             @(member.UserFullName ?? member.UserEmail ?? "Unknown")
 44:                                         </MudText>
 45:                                         @if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(member.OrganizationPositionFullName))
 46:                                         {
 47:                                             <MudText Typo="Typo.caption" Color="Color.Secondary">
 48:                                                 @member.OrganizationPositionFullName
 49:                                             </MudText>
 50:                                         }
 51:                                     </div>
 52:                                 </div>
 53:                                 <MudChip T="string"
 54:                                          Color="@RoleHelper.GetRoleColor(member.OrganizationRoleId)"
 55:                                          Size="Size.Small"
 56:                                          Variant="Variant.Filled">
 57:                                     @RoleHelper.GetRoleName(member.OrganizationRoleId)
 58:                                 </MudChip>
 59:                             </div>
 60:                         </MudListItem>
 61:                     }
 62:                 </MudList>
 63:             </MudPaper>
 64: 
 65:             @if (_members.Count > MaxPreviewCount)
 66:             {
 67:                 <MudText Typo="Typo.caption" Color="Color.Secondary" Align="Align.Center">
 68:                     Showing @MaxPreviewCount of @_members.Count members
 69:                 </MudText>
 70:             }
 71: 
 72:             <MudButton Variant="Variant.Outlined"
 73:                        Color="Color.Primary"
 74:                        StartIcon="@Icons.Material.Filled.People"
 75:                        OnClick="NavigateToMembers"
 76:                        FullWidth="true">
 77:                 Manage Members
 78:             </MudButton>
 79:         </MudStack>
 80:     }
 81: </div>
 82: 
 83: @code {
 84:     [Parameter, EditorRequired]
 85:     public Guid OrganizationId { get; set; }
 86: 
 87:     private const int MaxPreviewCount = 5;
 88: 
 89:     private List<OrganizationMemberDto> _members = new();
 90:     private bool _loading = true;
 91: 
 92:     protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
 93:     {
 94:         _loading = true;
 95:         try
 96:         {
 97:             var result = await MemberService.GetMembersAsync(OrganizationId);
 98:             _members = result?.ToList() ?? new List<OrganizationMemberDto>();
 99:         }
100:         finally
101:         {
102:             _loading = false;
103:         }
104:     }
105: 
106:     private static string GetInitial(OrganizationMemberDto member)
107:     {
108:         var name = member.UserFullName ?? member.UserEmail;
109:         return string.IsNullOrEmpty(name) ? "?" : name[..1].ToUpperInvariant();
110:     }
111: 
112:     private void NavigateToMembers()
113:     {
114:         Navigation.NavigateTo($"/organization/{OrganizationId}/members");
115:     }
116: }
````

## File: Explore.Blazor.Client/Components/Admin/Organization/OrganizationProfileSection.razor
````razor
  1: @* ABOUTME: Displays a read-only overview of organization profile information (name, contact, address, website). *@
  2: @* ABOUTME: Part of the Organization Admin Settings sidebar layout, with a link to the full profile page. *@
  3: 
  4: @using MudBlazor
  5: @using Explore.Blazor.Client.Services
  6: @inject IOrganizationService OrganizationService
  7: @inject NavigationManager Navigation
  8: 
  9: <div class="settings-section">
 10:     <div class="settings-section-header">
 11:         <MudText Typo="Typo.h5" Style="font-weight: 700;">Organization Profile</MudText>
 12:         <MudText Typo="Typo.body2" Color="Color.Secondary" Class="mt-1">
 13:             Overview of your organization's public profile information.
 14:         </MudText>
 15:     </div>
 16: 
 17:     @if (_loading)
 18:     {
 19:         <MudProgressCircular Color="Color.Primary" Indeterminate="true" Size="Size.Small" />
 20:     }
 21:     else if (_organization is null)
 22:     {
 23:         <MudAlert Severity="Severity.Warning" Variant="Variant.Outlined" Dense="true">
 24:             Organization profile could not be loaded.
 25:         </MudAlert>
 26:     }
 27:     else
 28:     {
 29:         <MudStack Spacing="3">
 30:             <MudPaper Elevation="0" Class="pa-4 border-solid border-1 mud-border-lines-default rounded-lg">
 31:                 <MudStack Spacing="2">
 32:                     <div class="d-flex align-center gap-2">
 33:                         <MudText Typo="Typo.h6" Style="font-weight: 600;">@_organization.FullName</MudText>
 34:                         @if (_organization.ApprovalStatusId == ApprovalStatusApproved)
 35:                         {
 36:                             <MudIcon Icon="@Icons.Material.Filled.Verified"
 37:                                      Color="Color.Primary"
 38:                                      Title="Verified"
 39:                                      Size="Size.Small" />
 40:                         }
 41:                     </div>
 42: 
 43:                     @if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(_organization.Email))
 44:                     {
 45:                         <div class="d-flex align-center gap-2">
 46:                             <MudIcon Icon="@Icons.Material.Filled.Email" Size="Size.Small" Color="Color.Secondary" />
 47:                             <MudText Typo="Typo.body2">@_organization.Email</MudText>
 48:                         </div>
 49:                     }
 50: 
 51:                     @if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(_organization.WebsiteUrl))
 52:                     {
 53:                         <div class="d-flex align-center gap-2">
 54:                             <MudIcon Icon="@Icons.Material.Filled.Language" Size="Size.Small" Color="Color.Secondary" />
 55:                             <MudLink Href="@_organization.WebsiteUrl" Target="_blank" Typo="Typo.body2" Color="Color.Primary">
 56:                                 @_organization.WebsiteUrl
 57:                             </MudLink>
 58:                         </div>
 59:                     }
 60: 
 61:                     @if (HasAddress)
 62:                     {
 63:                         <div class="d-flex align-center gap-2">
 64:                             <MudIcon Icon="@Icons.Material.Filled.LocationOn" Size="Size.Small" Color="Color.Secondary" />
 65:                             <MudText Typo="Typo.body2">@FormatAddress()</MudText>
 66:                         </div>
 67:                     }
 68:                 </MudStack>
 69:             </MudPaper>
 70: 
 71:             <MudButton Variant="Variant.Outlined"
 72:                        Color="Color.Primary"
 73:                        StartIcon="@Icons.Material.Filled.OpenInNew"
 74:                        OnClick="NavigateToProfile"
 75:                        FullWidth="true">
 76:                 View Full Profile
 77:             </MudButton>
 78:         </MudStack>
 79:     }
 80: </div>
 81: 
 82: @code {
 83:     [Parameter, EditorRequired]
 84:     public Guid OrganizationId { get; set; }
 85: 
 86:     private const int ApprovalStatusApproved = 2;
 87: 
 88:     private OrganizationDto? _organization;
 89:     private bool _loading = true;
 90: 
 91:     protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
 92:     {
 93:         _loading = true;
 94:         try
 95:         {
 96:             _organization = await OrganizationService.GetOrganizationByIdAsync(OrganizationId);
 97:         }
 98:         finally
 99:         {
100:             _loading = false;
101:         }
102:     }
103: 
104:     private bool HasAddress =>
105:         !string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(_organization?.Address) ||
106:         !string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(_organization?.City) ||
107:         !string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(_organization?.Country);
108: 
109:     private string FormatAddress()
110:     {
111:         var parts = new List<string>();
112: 
113:         if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(_organization?.Address))
114:             parts.Add(_organization.Address);
115:         if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(_organization?.City))
116:             parts.Add(_organization.City);
117:         if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(_organization?.Postcode))
118:             parts.Add(_organization.Postcode);
119:         if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(_organization?.Country))
120:             parts.Add(_organization.Country);
121: 
122:         return string.Join(", ", parts);
123:     }
124: 
125:     private void NavigateToProfile()
126:     {
127:         Navigation.NavigateTo($"/organization/{OrganizationId}");
128:     }
129: }
````

## File: Explore.Blazor.Client/Components/Admin/Organization/OrganizationVerificationSection.razor
````razor
  1: @* ABOUTME: Displays the organization's current verification/approval status with a colored badge. *@
  2: @* ABOUTME: Part of the Organization Admin Settings sidebar layout. Read-only for non-admin users. *@
  3: 
  4: @using MudBlazor
  5: @using Explore.Blazor.Client.Services
  6: @inject IOrganizationService OrganizationService
  7: 
  8: <div class="settings-section">
  9:     <div class="settings-section-header">
 10:         <MudText Typo="Typo.h5" Style="font-weight: 700;">Verification Status</MudText>
 11:         <MudText Typo="Typo.body2" Color="Color.Secondary" Class="mt-1">
 12:             Your organization's approval and verification standing.
 13:         </MudText>
 14:     </div>
 15: 
 16:     @if (_loading)
 17:     {
 18:         <MudProgressCircular Color="Color.Primary" Indeterminate="true" Size="Size.Small" />
 19:     }
 20:     else if (_organization is null)
 21:     {
 22:         <MudAlert Severity="Severity.Warning" Variant="Variant.Outlined" Dense="true">
 23:             Verification status could not be loaded.
 24:         </MudAlert>
 25:     }
 26:     else
 27:     {
 28:         <MudStack Spacing="3">
 29:             <MudPaper Elevation="0" Class="pa-4 border-solid border-1 mud-border-lines-default rounded-lg">
 30:                 <MudStack Spacing="3">
 31:                     <div class="d-flex align-center gap-3">
 32:                         <MudIcon Icon="@GetStatusIcon()" Color="@GetStatusColor()" Size="Size.Medium" />
 33:                         <div>
 34:                             <MudText Typo="Typo.subtitle1" Style="font-weight: 600;">
 35:                                 @GetStatusLabel()
 36:                             </MudText>
 37:                             <MudText Typo="Typo.caption" Color="Color.Secondary">
 38:                                 @(_organization.ApprovalStatusFullName ?? "Unknown status")
 39:                             </MudText>
 40:                         </div>
 41:                         <MudSpacer />
 42:                         <MudChip T="string"
 43:                                  Color="@GetStatusColor()"
 44:                                  Size="Size.Small"
 45:                                  Variant="Variant.Filled">
 46:                             @GetStatusLabel()
 47:                         </MudChip>
 48:                     </div>
 49: 
 50:                     <MudDivider />
 51: 
 52:                     <MudText Typo="Typo.body2" Color="Color.Secondary">
 53:                         @GetStatusDescription()
 54:                     </MudText>
 55:                 </MudStack>
 56:             </MudPaper>
 57: 
 58:             <MudAlert Severity="Severity.Info" Variant="Variant.Outlined" Dense="true" Icon="@Icons.Material.Filled.Info">
 59:                 Verification is managed by platform administrators. Verified organizations receive a badge
 60:                 on their public profile and gain access to additional features.
 61:             </MudAlert>
 62:         </MudStack>
 63:     }
 64: </div>
 65: 
 66: @code {
 67:     [Parameter, EditorRequired]
 68:     public Guid OrganizationId { get; set; }
 69: 
 70:     private const int StatusPending = 1;
 71:     private const int StatusApproved = 2;
 72:     private const int StatusRejected = 3;
 73: 
 74:     private OrganizationDto? _organization;
 75:     private bool _loading = true;
 76: 
 77:     protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
 78:     {
 79:         _loading = true;
 80:         try
 81:         {
 82:             _organization = await OrganizationService.GetOrganizationByIdAsync(OrganizationId);
 83:         }
 84:         finally
 85:         {
 86:             _loading = false;
 87:         }
 88:     }
 89: 
 90:     private string GetStatusLabel() => _organization?.ApprovalStatusId switch
 91:     {
 92:         StatusPending => "Pending",
 93:         StatusApproved => "Approved",
 94:         StatusRejected => "Rejected",
 95:         _ => "Unknown"
 96:     };
 97: 
 98:     private Color GetStatusColor() => _organization?.ApprovalStatusId switch
 99:     {
100:         StatusPending => Color.Warning,
101:         StatusApproved => Color.Success,
102:         StatusRejected => Color.Error,
103:         _ => Color.Default
104:     };
105: 
106:     private string GetStatusIcon() => _organization?.ApprovalStatusId switch
107:     {
108:         StatusPending => Icons.Material.Filled.HourglassTop,
109:         StatusApproved => Icons.Material.Filled.Verified,
110:         StatusRejected => Icons.Material.Filled.Cancel,
111:         _ => Icons.Material.Filled.HelpOutline
112:     };
113: 
114:     private string GetStatusDescription() => _organization?.ApprovalStatusId switch
115:     {
116:         StatusPending => "Your organization is currently under review. This process typically takes a few business days.",
117:         StatusApproved => "Your organization has been verified and approved. A verification badge is displayed on your public profile.",
118:         StatusRejected => "Your organization's verification request was not approved. Please contact support for more information.",
119:         _ => "The current verification status could not be determined."
120:     };
121: }

## File: Explore.Blazor.Client/Components/Admin/Tenant/TenantAdminSettingsLayout.razor
````razor
  1: @* ABOUTME: Sidebar layout component for Tenant Admin Settings. *@
  2: @* ABOUTME: Provides Google-style sidebar navigation for tenant-level policy, domain, and branding settings. *@
  3: 
  4: @using MudBlazor
  5: @using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components
  6: @using Explore.Blazor.Client.Services
  7: 
  8: @inject ITenantOnboardingService TenantOnboardingService
  9: @inject ISnackbar Snackbar
 10: 
 11: <div class="settings-layout">
 12:     <MudContainer MaxWidth="MaxWidth.Large" Class="py-8">
 13:         <!-- Header -->
 14:         <div class="settings-header mb-8">
 15:             <MudText Typo="Typo.h4" Style="font-weight: 800;">Tenant Settings</MudText>
 16:             <MudText Typo="Typo.body2" Color="Color.Secondary" Class="mt-2">Manage tenant-level policy, domain, and branding settings</MudText>
 17:         </div>
 18: 
 19:         @if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(_errorMessage))
 20:         {
 21:             <MudAlert Severity="Severity.Error" Class="mb-4">@_errorMessage</MudAlert>
 22:         }
 23: 
 24:         @if (_isLoading)
 25:         {
 26:             <MudStack AlignItems="AlignItems.Center" Class="py-12">
 27:                 <MudProgressCircular Indeterminate="true" Color="Color.Primary" />
 28:                 <MudText Typo="Typo.body2" Color="Color.Secondary" Class="mt-4">Loading tenant settings...</MudText>
 29:             </MudStack>
 30:         }
 31:         else if (!_canEdit)
 32:         {
 33:             <MudAlert Severity="Severity.Warning" Class="mb-4">
 34:                 You do not have tenant administrator permissions to view or modify these settings.
 35:             </MudAlert>
 36:         }
 37:         else
 38:         {
 39:             <!-- Main Layout: Sidebar + Content -->
 40:             <MudGrid Spacing="4">
 41:                 <!-- Sidebar Navigation -->
 42:                 <MudItem xs="12" sm="12" md="3">
 43:                     <MudPaper Elevation="0" Class="settings-sidebar pa-0 rounded-lg border-solid border-1 mud-border-lines-default">
 44:                         <MudList T="string" Dense="false" DisablePadding="true">
 45:                             <MudListItem Icon="@Icons.Material.Filled.Policy"
 46:                                          Text="Policies"
 47:                                          Class="@GetNavItemClass("policies")"
 48:                                          OnClick="@(() => SelectSection("policies"))" />
 49:                             <MudListItem Icon="@Icons.Material.Filled.Language"
 50:                                          Text="Domain"
 51:                                          Class="@GetNavItemClass("domain")"
 52:                                          OnClick="@(() => SelectSection("domain"))" />
 53:                             <MudListItem Icon="@Icons.Material.Filled.Palette"
 54:                                          Text="Branding"
 55:                                          Class="@GetNavItemClass("branding")"
 56:                                          OnClick="@(() => SelectSection("branding"))" />
 57:                         </MudList>
 58:                     </MudPaper>
 59:                 </MudItem>
 60: 
 61:                 <!-- Content Area -->
 62:                 <MudItem xs="12" sm="12" md="9">
 63:                     <MudPaper Elevation="0" Class="settings-content pa-6 rounded-lg border-solid border-1 mud-border-lines-default">
 64:                         @if (_currentSection == "policies")
 65:                         {
 66:                             <TenantPoliciesSection Model="_model" />
 67:                         }
 68:                         else if (_currentSection == "domain")
 69:                         {
 70:                             <TenantDomainSection Model="_model" />
 71:                         }
 72:                         else if (_currentSection == "branding")
 73:                         {
 74:                             <TenantBrandingSection Model="_model" />
 75:                         }
 76: 
 77:                         <MudDivider Class="my-4" />
 78: 
 79:                         <MudStack Row="true" Justify="Justify.FlexEnd">
 80:                             <MudButton Variant="Variant.Filled"
 81:                                        Color="Color.Primary"
 82:                                        OnClick="SaveAsync"
 83:                                        Disabled="_isSaving"
 84:                                        StartIcon="@(_isSaving ? Icons.Material.Filled.HourglassEmpty : Icons.Material.Filled.Save)">
 85:                                 @(_isSaving ? "Saving..." : "Save Tenant Settings")
 86:                             </MudButton>
 87:                         </MudStack>
 88:                     </MudPaper>
 89:                 </MudItem>
 90:             </MudGrid>
 91:         }
 92:     </MudContainer>
 93: </div>
 94: 
 95: @code {
 96:     private TenantPolicySettingsModel _model = new();
 97:     private bool _isLoading = true;
 98:     private bool _isSaving;
 99:     private bool _canEdit;
100:     private string? _errorMessage;
101:     private string _currentSection = "policies";
102: 
103:     protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
104:     {
105:         var status = await TenantOnboardingService.GetStatusAsync();
106:         _canEdit = status?.IsCurrentUserTenantAdministrator == true
107:                 || status?.IsCurrentUserInstanceAdministrator == true;
108: 
109:         if (!_canEdit)
110:         {
111:             _isLoading = false;
112:             return;
113:         }
114: 
115:         _model = await TenantOnboardingService.GetSettingsAsync();
116:         _isLoading = false;
117:     }
118: 
119:     private async Task SaveAsync()
120:     {
121:         _isSaving = true;
122:         _errorMessage = null;
123: 
124:         var response = await TenantOnboardingService.UpdateSettingsAsync(_model);
125:         _isSaving = false;
126: 
127:         if (response.Success)
128:         {
129:             Snackbar.Add("Tenant settings saved.", Severity.Success);
130:             return;
131:         }
132: 
133:         _errorMessage = string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(response.Message)
134:             ? "Failed to save tenant settings."
135:             : response.Message;
136:     }
137: 
138:     private void SelectSection(string section)
139:     {
140:         _currentSection = section;
141:     }
142: 
143:     private string GetNavItemClass(string section)
144:     {
145:         return _currentSection == section ? "settings-nav-active" : "";
146:     }
147: }
````

## File: Explore.Blazor.Client/Components/Admin/Tenant/TenantBrandingSection.razor
````razor
 1: @* ABOUTME: Renders tenant branding fields for the Tenant Admin Settings sidebar. *@
 2: @* ABOUTME: Includes brand name, logo, favicon, and custom CSS URL fields with instance-level lock support. *@

38:                       Variant="Variant.Outlined"

52:         !Model.CanOverrideBrandFaviconUrl ||

54: }

## File: Explore.Blazor.Client/Components/Admin/Tenant/TenantPoliciesSection.razor
````razor
 1: @* ABOUTME: Renders event and organization policy settings for the Tenant Admin Settings sidebar. *@
 2: @* ABOUTME: Includes user submission, approval, and verification switches with instance-level lock support. *@
 3: 
 4: @using MudBlazor
 5: @using Explore.Blazor.Client.Services
 6: 
 7: <div class="settings-section">
 8:     <div class="settings-section-header">
 9:         <MudText Typo="Typo.h5" Style="font-weight: 700;">Event & Organization Policies</MudText>
10:         <MudText Typo="Typo.body2" Color="Color.Secondary" Class="mt-1">
11:             Control how events are submitted, approved, and how organizations are verified.
12:         </MudText>
13:     </div>
14:     <MudStack Spacing="3">
15:         <MudSwitch T="bool" @bind-Value="Model.AllowUserSubmittedEvents" Color="Color.Primary">
16:             Allow users to submit events
17:         </MudSwitch>
18: 
19:         <MudSwitch T="bool" @bind-Value="Model.RequireEventApproval" Color="Color.Primary">
20:             Require approval before publication
21:         </MudSwitch>
22: 
23:         <MudSwitch T="bool"
24:                    @bind-Value="Model.RequireOrganizationVerification"
25:                    Color="Color.Primary"
26:                    Disabled="@(!Model.CanTenantOmitVerification)">
27:             Require organization verification
28:         </MudSwitch>
29: 
30:         @if (!Model.CanTenantOmitVerification)
31:         {
32:             <MudText Typo="Typo.caption" Color="Color.Warning">
33:                 Verification requirement is locked by instance policy.
34:             </MudText>
35:         }
36:     </MudStack>
37: </div>
38: 
39: @code {
40:     [Parameter, EditorRequired]
41:     public TenantPolicySettingsModel Model { get; set; } = null!;
42: }
````

## File: .claude/skills/auth-patterns/resources/user-id-extraction.md
````markdown
  1: # User ID Extraction Pattern
  2: 
  3: This document details the **CRITICAL** pattern for safely and consistently extracting the user ID from JWT claims within the ISLAMU Event platform. This pattern accounts for various claim types and provides a robust fallback mechanism.
  4: 
  5: ---
  6: 
  7: ## 1. The Fallback Pattern (ASP.NET Core)
  8: 
  9: Always use this specific fallback logic when attempting to retrieve the authenticated user's ID from a `ClaimsPrincipal` (e.g., `HttpContext.User`).
 10: 
 11: ```csharp
 12: using System.Security.Claims; // Required for ClaimTypes
 13: 
 14: // Access the ClaimsPrincipal from HttpContext or another source
 15: // Example from an ASP.NET Core Controller:
 16: var claimsPrincipal = HttpContext.User;
 17: 
 18: var userId = claimsPrincipal.FindFirst("sub")?.Value // 1. Standard OIDC subject claim (preferred)
 19:     ?? claimsPrincipal.FindFirst("http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/nameidentifier")?.Value // 2. Legacy .NET nameidentifier claim (fallback)
 20:     ?? claimsPrincipal.FindFirst("sid")?.Value; // 3. Session ID (last resort, less common for user ID)
 21: 
 22: if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(userId))
 23: {
 24:     // Handle the case where no user ID could be extracted.
 25:     // This typically indicates a misconfigured token or an unauthenticated request
 26:     // that reached an [Authorize] endpoint without a valid user context.
 27:     // Depending on context (e.g., API controller), you might return Unauthorized.
 28:     // In a Blazor component, you might redirect to login.
 29:     throw new UnauthorizedAccessException("User ID claim could not be found in the token.");
 30: }
 31: 
 32: // At this point, userId contains the extracted user ID
 33: Console.WriteLine($"Extracted User ID: {userId}");
 34: ```
 35: 
 36: ### Claim Priority Explained:
 37: 
 38: 1.  **`sub` (Subject)**: This is the **standard and preferred** claim for a unique identifier of the user (or "subject") in OpenID Connect (OIDC) and OAuth 2.0. Keycloak typically populates this.
 39: 2.  **`http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/nameidentifier`**: This is the .NET Framework's default claim type for `NameIdentifier` (User ID). It's a common fallback, especially when dealing with older identity providers or configurations.
 40: 3.  **`sid` (Session ID)**: This is the session ID claim. While it's a unique identifier for a session, it's generally **less preferred** for identifying the user directly across different sessions or systems. It's included as a last resort fallback if `sub` and `nameidentifier` are absent, but its usage as a primary user ID should be carefully evaluated based on the specific requirements.
 41: 
 42: ---
 43: 
 44: ## 2. Using the Pattern in MediatR Handlers
 45: 
 46: When performing authorization checks or data filtering based on the current user in MediatR handlers, the user ID typically needs to be passed from the controller (where `HttpContext` is available) to the handler.
 47: 
 48: ```csharp
 49: // File: Explore.API/Controllers/EventController.cs
 50: using MediatR;
 51: using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authorization;
 52: using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;
 53: using System.Security.Claims; // For ClaimsPrincipal and ClaimTypes
 54: 
 55: [Authorize]
 56: [HttpPost]
 57: public async Task<ActionResult<BaseCommandResponse<Guid>>> CreateEvent([FromBody] CreateEventDto dto)
 58: {
 59:     // ✅ Extract user ID using the fallback pattern
 60:     var userId = HttpContext.User.FindFirst("sub")?.Value
 61:         ?? HttpContext.User.FindFirst(ClaimTypes.NameIdentifier)?.Value // Using ClaimTypes.NameIdentifier constant
 62:         ?? HttpContext.User.FindFirst("sid")?.Value;
 63: 
 64:     if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(userId))
 65:     {
 66:         return Unauthorized(new { error = "User ID not found in token" });
 67:     }
 68: 
 69:     // Pass the extracted userId to the command
 70:     var command = new CreateEventCommand { EventDto = dto, UserId = userId }; // Assume CreateEventCommand has a UserId property
 71:     var response = await _mediator.Send(command);
 72:     return Ok(response);
 73: }
 74: 
 75: // File: Explore.Application/Features/Events/Requests/Commands/CreateEventCommand.cs
 76: public class CreateEventCommand : IRequest<BaseCommandResponse<Guid>>
 77: {
 78:     public CreateEventDto EventDto { get; set; }
 79:     public string UserId { get; set; } = string.Empty; // ✅ Property to receive the userId
 80: }
 81: 
 82: // File: Explore.Application/Features/Events/Handlers/Commands/CreateEventCommandHandler.cs
 83: public class CreateEventCommandHandler : IRequestHandler<CreateEventCommand, BaseCommandResponse<Guid>>
 84: {
 85:     // ... dependencies ...
 86: 
 87:     public async Task<BaseCommandResponse<Guid>> Handle(CreateEventCommand request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
 88:     {
 89:         // ... validation ...
 90:         
 91:         // ✅ Use request.UserId for ownership checks or data filtering
 92:         var isAuthorized = await _permissionService.HasPermission(request.UserId, "create_event");
 93:         if (!isAuthorized)
 94:         {
 95:             // Handle unauthorized access within the application layer
 96:             // For example, return a specific error in BaseCommandResponse
 97:         }
 98: 
 99:         // ... create event logic ...
100:     }
101: }
102: ```
103: 
104: ---
105: 
106: ## 3. Key Considerations
107: 
108: *   **Security**: Always perform server-side validation of user claims. Do not trust client-side assertions.
109: *   **Consistency**: Adhere strictly to this pattern across all services that require user ID extraction.
110: *   **Error Handling**: Ensure that `string.IsNullOrEmpty(userId)` is handled appropriately (e.g., returning `401 Unauthorized` from an API controller).
111: *   **Blazor vs. API**: In Blazor Server-side, `HttpContext.User` is directly available. In Blazor WebAssembly, you typically rely on the BFF pattern, where the server-side Blazor app handles authentication and potentially passes claims to the WASM client.
112: 
113: ---
114: 
115: **Related Skills**:
116: - [`auth-patterns`](../SKILL.md) - General authentication and authorization rules.
117: - [`blazor-bff-patterns`](../../blazor-bff-patterns/SKILL.md) - Blazor-specific authentication context.
118: - [`cqrs-mediatr-guidelines`](../../cqrs-mediatr-guidelines/SKILL.md) - How to pass user context to MediatR handlers.
````

## File: .claude/skills/prd/SKILL.md
````markdown
  1: ---
  2: name: prd
  3: description: "Generate a Product Requirements Document (PRD) for a new feature. Use when planning a feature, starting a new project, or when asked to create a PRD. Triggers on: create a prd, write prd for, plan this feature, requirements for, spec out."
  4: ---
  5: 
  6: # PRD Generator
  7: 
  8: Create detailed Product Requirements Documents that are clear, actionable, and suitable for implementation.
  9: 
 10: ---
 11: 
 12: ## The Job
 13: 
 14: 1. Receive a feature description from the user
 15: 2. Ask 3-5 essential clarifying questions (with lettered options)
 16: 3. Generate a structured PRD based on answers
 17: 4. Save to `dev/active/prd.md`
 18: 
 19: **Important:** Do NOT start implementing. Just create the PRD.
 20: 
 21: ---
 22: 
 23: ## Step 1: Clarifying Questions
 24: 
 25: Ask only critical questions where the initial prompt is ambiguous. Focus on:
 26: 
 27: - **Problem/Goal:** What problem does this solve?
 28: - **Core Functionality:** What are the key actions?
 29: - **Scope/Boundaries:** What should it NOT do?
 30: - **Success Criteria:** How do we know it's done?
 31: 
 32: ### Format Questions Like This:
 33: 
 34: ```
 35: 1. What is the primary goal of this feature?
 36:    A. Improve user onboarding experience
 37:    B. Increase user retention
 38:    C. Reduce support burden
 39:    D. Other: [please specify]
 40: 
 41: 2. Who is the target user?
 42:    A. New users only
 43:    B. Existing users only
 44:    C. All users
 45:    D. Admin users only
 46: 
 47: 3. What is the scope?
 48:    A. Minimal viable version
 49:    B. Full-featured implementation
 50:    C. Just the backend/API
 51:    D. Just the UI
 52: ```
 53: 
 54: This lets users respond with "1A, 2C, 3B" for quick iteration.
 55: 
 56: ---
 57: 
 58: ## Step 2: PRD Structure
 59: 
 60: Generate the PRD with these sections:
 61: 
 62: ### 1. Introduction/Overview
 63: 
 64: Brief description of the feature and the problem it solves.
 65: 
 66: ### 2. Goals
 67: 
 68: Specific, measurable objectives (bullet list).
 69: 
 70: ### 3. User Stories
 71: 
 72: Each story needs:
 73: 
 74: - **Title:** Short descriptive name
 75: - **Description:** "As a [user], I want [feature] so that [benefit]"
 76: - **Acceptance Criteria:** Verifiable checklist of what "done" means
 77: 
 78: Each story should be small enough to implement in one focused session.
 79: 
 80: **Format:**
 81: 
 82: ```markdown
 83: ### US-001: [Title]
 84: 
 85: **Description:** As a [user], I want [feature] so that [benefit].
 86: 
 87: **Acceptance Criteria:**
 88: 
 89: - [ ] Specific verifiable criterion
 90: - [ ] Another criterion
 91: - [ ] Typecheck/lint passes
 92: - [ ] **[UI stories only]** Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
 93: ```
 94: 
 95: **Important:**
 96: 
 97: - Acceptance criteria must be verifiable, not vague. "Works correctly" is bad. "Button shows confirmation dialog before deleting" is good.
 98: - **For any story with UI changes:** Always include "Verify in browser using dev-browser skill" as acceptance criteria. This ensures visual verification of frontend work.
 99: 
100: ### 4. Functional Requirements
101: 
102: Numbered list of specific functionalities:
103: 
104: - "FR-1: The system must allow users to..."
105: - "FR-2: When a user clicks X, the system must..."
106: 
107: Be explicit and unambiguous.
108: 
109: ### 5. Non-Goals (Out of Scope)
110: 
111: What this feature will NOT include. Critical for managing scope.
112: 
113: ### 6. Design Considerations (Optional)
114: 
115: - UI/UX requirements
116: - Link to mockups if available
117: - Relevant existing components to reuse
118: 
119: ### 7. Technical Considerations (Optional)
120: 
121: - Known constraints or dependencies
122: - Integration points with existing systems
123: - Performance requirements
124: 
125: ### 8. Success Metrics
126: 
127: How will success be measured?
128: 
129: - "Reduce time to complete X by 50%"
130: - "Increase conversion rate by 10%"
131: 
132: ### 9. Open Questions
133: 
134: Remaining questions or areas needing clarification.
135: 
136: ---
137: 
138: ## Writing for Junior Developers
139: 
140: The PRD reader may be a junior developer or AI agent. Therefore:
141: 
142: - Be explicit and unambiguous
143: - Avoid jargon or explain it
144: - Provide enough detail to understand purpose and core logic
145: - Number requirements for easy reference
146: - Use concrete examples where helpful
147: 
148: ---
149: 
150: ## Archiving Previous PRDs
151: 
152: **Before writing a new `dev/active/prd.md`, check if there is an existing one from a different feature:**
153: 
154: 1. Read the current `dev/active/prd.md` if it exists
155: 2. Check if it's for a different feature than what you're about to create
156: 3. If different:
157:    - Extract feature name from PRD title/intro
158:    - Check if archive folder already exists: look for `dev/archive/*-feature-name/`
159:    - If found, use existing folder; if not, create `dev/archive/YYYY-MM-DD-feature-name/`
160:    - Copy current `dev/active/prd.md` to archive folder
161:    - Write the new PRD to `dev/active/prd.md`
162: 
163: **Shared archive folders:** Multiple runs of same feature (across dates) share one archive folder. Prevents duplicate archives when PRD skill and task skill run on different days.
164: 
165: ---
166: 
167: ## Output
168: 
169: - **Format:** Markdown (`.md`)
170: - **Location:** `dev/active/`
171: - **Filename:** `dev/active/prd.md`
172: 
173: ---
174: 
175: ## Example PRD
176: 
177: ```markdown
178: # PRD: Task Priority System
179: 
180: ## Introduction
181: 
182: Add priority levels to tasks so users can focus on what matters most. Tasks can be marked as high, medium, or low priority, with visual indicators and filtering to help users manage their workload effectively.
183: 
184: ## Goals
185: 
186: - Allow assigning priority (high/medium/low) to any task
187: - Provide clear visual differentiation between priority levels
188: - Enable filtering and sorting by priority
189: - Default new tasks to medium priority
190: 
191: ## User Stories
192: 
193: ### US-001: Add priority field to database
194: 
195: **Description:** As a developer, I need to store task priority so it persists across sessions.
196: 
197: **Acceptance Criteria:**
198: 
199: - [ ] Add priority column to tasks table: 'high' | 'medium' | 'low' (default 'medium')
200: - [ ] Generate and run migration successfully
201: - [ ] Typecheck passes
202: 
203: ### US-002: Display priority indicator on task cards
204: 
205: **Description:** As a user, I want to see task priority at a glance so I know what needs attention first.
206: 
207: **Acceptance Criteria:**
208: 
209: - [ ] Each task card shows colored priority badge (red=high, yellow=medium, gray=low)
210: - [ ] Priority visible without hovering or clicking
211: 
212: ### US-003: Add priority selector to task edit
213: 
214: **Description:** As a user, I want to change a task's priority when editing it.
215: 
216: **Acceptance Criteria:**
217: 
218: - [ ] Priority dropdown in task edit modal
219: - [ ] Shows current priority as selected
220: - [ ] Saves immediately on selection change
221: 
222: ### US-004: Filter tasks by priority
223: 
224: **Description:** As a user, I want to filter the task list to see only high-priority items when I'm focused.
225: 
226: **Acceptance Criteria:**
227: 
228: - [ ] Filter dropdown with options: All | High | Medium | Low
229: - [ ] Filter persists in URL params
230: - [ ] Empty state message when no tasks match filter
231: 
232: ## Functional Requirements
233: 
234: - FR-1: Add `priority` field to tasks table ('high' | 'medium' | 'low', default 'medium')
235: - FR-2: Display colored priority badge on each task card
236: - FR-3: Include priority selector in task edit modal
237: - FR-4: Add priority filter dropdown to task list header
238: - FR-5: Sort by priority within each status column (high to medium to low)
239: 
240: ## Non-Goals
241: 
242: - No priority-based notifications or reminders
243: - No automatic priority assignment based on due date
244: - No priority inheritance for subtasks
245: 
246: ## Technical Considerations
247: 
248: - Reuse existing badge component with color variants
249: - Filter state managed via URL search params
250: - Priority stored in database, not computed
251: 
252: ## Success Metrics
253: 
254: - Users can change priority in under 2 clicks
255: - High-priority tasks immediately visible at top of lists
256: - No regression in task list performance
257: 
258: ## Open Questions
259: 
260: - Should priority affect task ordering within a column?
261: - Should we add keyboard shortcuts for priority changes?
262: ```
263: 
264: ---
265: 
266: ## Checklist
267: 
268: Before saving the PRD:
269: 
270: - [ ] **Archived previous PRD** (if `dev/active/prd.md` exists for a different feature, archive it first)
271: - [ ] Asked clarifying questions with lettered options
272: - [ ] Incorporated user's answers
273: - [ ] User stories are small and specific
274: - [ ] Functional requirements are numbered and unambiguous
275: - [ ] Non-goals section defines clear boundaries
276: - [ ] Saved to `dev/active/prd.md`
````

 95: ## Files to Modify (4)
 96: 
 97: 1. **Routes.razor** — Add 11 routes (3 settings + 8 lookup tables) with guards

101:    - Add settings routes + all lookup table routes

103: 2. **NavMenu.razor** — Add Instance Settings + Tenant Settings links in admin dropdown
104: 
105: 3. **AdminList.razor** — Add Settings cards section before Lookup Tables section
106: 
107: 4. **InstanceSettings.razor** and **TenantPolicySettings.razor** — Remove @page directives (replaced by new files) or delete entirely
108: 
109: ## Key Patterns to Follow
110: 
111: ### Sidebar Pattern (from SettingsLayout.razor)
112: ```razor
113: <MudGrid Spacing="4">
114:     <MudItem xs="12" sm="12" md="3">
115:         <MudPaper Elevation="0" Class="settings-sidebar pa-0 rounded-lg border-solid border-1 mud-border-lines-default">
116:             <MudList T="string" Dense="false" DisablePadding="true">
117:                 <MudListItem Icon="@Icons.Material.Filled.Tune"
118:                              Text="Section Name"
119:                              Class="@GetNavItemClass("section-key")"
120:                              OnClick="@(() => SelectSection("section-key"))" />
121:             </MudList>
122:         </MudPaper>
123:     </MudItem>
124:     <MudItem xs="12" sm="12" md="9">
125:         <MudPaper Elevation="0" Class="settings-content pa-6 rounded-lg border-solid border-1 mud-border-lines-default">
126:             @if (CurrentSection == "section-key") { <SectionComponent Model="_model" /> }
127:         </MudPaper>
128:     </MudItem>
129: </MudGrid>
130: ```
131: 
132: ### Section Component Pattern
133: ```razor
134: @* ABOUTME: Description *@
135: @* ABOUTME: Part of the X Admin Settings sidebar layout *@
136: @using MudBlazor
137: @using Explore.Blazor.Client.Services
138: 
139: <div class="settings-section">
140:     <div class="settings-section-header">
141:         <MudText Typo="Typo.h5" Style="font-weight: 700;">Title</MudText>
142:         <MudText Typo="Typo.body2" Color="Color.Secondary" Class="mt-1">Description</MudText>
143:     </div>
144:     <MudStack Spacing="3">
145:         <!-- form fields -->
146:     </MudStack>
147: </div>
148: 
149: @code {
150:     [Parameter, EditorRequired]
151:     public ModelType Model { get; set; } = null!;
152: }
153: ```
154: 
155: ## Services — No New Services Needed
156: - Instance: `IInstanceOnboardingService` (GetStatusAsync, GetSettingsAsync, UpdateSettingsAsync)
157: - Tenant: `ITenantOnboardingService` (GetStatusAsync, GetSettingsAsync, UpdateSettingsAsync)
158: - Organization: `IOrganizationService` (GetOrganizationByIdAsync), `IOrganizationMemberService` (GetMembersAsync)
159: - Shared: `RoleHelper` from `Explore.Blazor.Client.Helpers` for role colors/names
160: 
161: ## Key Models
162: - `InstanceGovernanceSettingsModel` — in `InstanceOnboardingService.cs`
163: - `TenantPolicySettingsModel` — in `TenantOnboardingService.cs`
164: - `InstanceOnboardingStatusModel` — has `IsCurrentUserInstanceAdmin`
165: - `TenantOnboardingStatusModel` — has `IsCurrentUserTenantAdministrator`, `IsCurrentUserInstanceAdministrator`
166: - `OrganizationDto` — from generated `EventApiClient.g.cs` (ApprovalStatusId, FullName, Email, etc.)
167: - `OrganizationMemberDto` — UserFullName, UserEmail, OrganizationRoleId, OrganizationPositionFullName
168: 
169: ## Quick Resume Checklist
170: 
171: 1. Read this context file
172: 2. Read the plan: `polished-sparking-goose.md`
173: 3. Build first: `dotnet build --configuration Release --verbosity quiet`
174: 4. Create files in order: Instance sections → Instance layout+CSS+page → Tenant sections → Tenant layout+CSS+page → Org sections → Org layout+CSS+page
175: 5. Update Routes.razor, NavMenu.razor, AdminList.razor
176: 6. Remove @page from old InstanceSettings.razor and TenantPolicySettings.razor (or delete them)
177: 7. Build and run all tests
````

## File: dev/active/admin-hierarchy-pages/admin-hierarchy-pages-plan.md
````markdown
  1: # Plan: Admin Hierarchy Pages (Instance, Tenant, Organization)
  2: 
  3: Last Updated: 2026-02-08
  4: 
  5: ## Executive Summary
  6: 
  7: This implementation introduces three separate admin experiences with strict authority boundaries:
  8: 
  9: 1. Instance Administrator pages for platform-wide governance.
 10: 2. Tenant Administrator pages for tenant policy and moderation controls.
 11: 3. Organization Administrator pages for organization operations and membership management.
 12: 
 13: The work will align the current codebase with project documentation around hierarchy, tenancy, runtime deployment switching, and lock-aware settings. The final outcome is enterprise-grade, maintainable, and follows Clean Architecture (Domain -> Application -> Infrastructure/Persistence -> API/BFF -> Blazor UI).
 14: 
 15: This plan is explicitly designed for the requirements:
 16: 
 17: - Instance admin can switch single-tenant and multi-tenant mode at runtime.
 18: - Instance admin can govern event/module aspects available to tenants.
 19: - Tenant admin can control user-submitted events, verification workflow behavior, and moderation defaults.
 20: - Tenant admin can manage whether verification requirements are enforced or omitted (if delegation allows it).
 21: - Admin experiences are different by role and by scope.
 22: 
 23: ## Current State Analysis
 24: 
 25: ## Documentation Intent (Target Behavior)
 26: 
 27: The following docs establish expected behavior:
 28: 
 29: - `docs/ADMIN_HIERARCHY.md`
 30: - `docs/MULTI_TENANCY.md`
 31: - `docs/DEPLOYMENT_MODES.md`
 32: - `docs/OPERATIONS.md`
 33: - `docs/EXTENSIBILITY.md`
 34: - `docs/MODULAR_EVENTS.md`
 35: - `docs/RENDER_POLICIES.md`
 36: - `docs/SECURITY.md`
 37: 
 38: Expected system characteristics from docs:
 39: 
 40: - Scope-separated admin authority (instance vs tenant vs organization).
 41: - Cascading settings with lock/delegation semantics.
 42: - Runtime deployment mode switching.
 43: - Tenant/module governance with constraints.
 44: - Strict cross-tenant isolation.
 45: 
 46: ## Observed Codebase Reality (As-Is)
 47: 
 48: ### Blazor Admin UX
 49: 
 50: - Main admin page is currently centralized:
 51:   - `Explore.Blazor.Client/Pages/Admin/AdminList.razor`

 53:   - `Explore.Blazor.Client/Layout/NavMenu.razor`
 54:   - `Explore.Blazor.Client/Layout/NavMenu.razor.cs`
 55: - Routing uses manual route registration and is incomplete relative to existing pages:
 56:   - `Explore.Blazor/Components/Routes.razor`

 58: ### API Authorization

 67: ### Tenancy and Runtime Deployment Mode

 70:   - `Explore.API/Services/TenantContext.cs`
 71:   - `Explore.Infrastructure/DeploymentSettings.cs`

 76: ### Settings and Governance Foundation

 80: - `Explore.Domain/SystemSetting.cs`

 85:

 90: - Existing flows do not expose role-specific governance UIs/APIs.
 91: 
 92: ## Key Gaps to Close
 93: 
 94: 1. Replace coarse admin role handling with scope-specific policy enforcement.
 95: 2. Create role-specific admin portals/routes/pages.
 96: 3. Make runtime deployment mode switching truly settings-driven.
 97: 4. Remove static tenant header assumptions in multi-tenant operational flows.
 98: 5. Formalize lock/delegation UX and API semantics.
 99: 6. Fill testing matrix for role/scope/isolation correctness.
100: 
101: ## Proposed Future State
102: 
103: ## Role-Separated Admin Portals
104: 
105: ### 1) Instance Administrator Portal
106: 
107: Route group:
108: 
109: - `/admin/instance/*`
110: 
111: Primary capabilities:
112: 
113: - Runtime deployment mode switch (`SingleTenant` <-> `MultiTenant`).
114: - Global tenant registration and onboarding policy controls.
115: - Global module catalog governance.
116: - System lock/delegation configuration for tenant-overridable settings.
117: - Platform-level configuration audit visibility.
118: 
119: ### 2) Tenant Administrator Portal
120: 
121: Route group:
122: 
123: - `/admin/tenant/*`
124: 
125: Primary capabilities:
126: 
127: - User-submitted event policy controls.
128: - Organization verification policy controls.
129: - Tenant-level module enablement from allowed global set.
130: - Tenant-level moderation defaults and policy overrides (when unlocked).
131: 
132: ### 3) Organization Administrator Portal
133: 
134: Route group:
135: 
136: - `/admin/organization/{organizationId}/*`
137: 
138: Primary capabilities:
139: 
140: - Organization member/role management.
141: - Organization profile and operational settings.
142: - Organization verification submission and status visibility.
143: - Organization-level event defaults within tenant policy boundaries.
144: 
145: ## Settings and Policy Cascade Model
146: 
147: Resolution order:
148: 
149: 1. System default (`SystemSetting`).
150: 2. System lock/delegation state (`IsLocked` + metadata).
151: 3. Tenant override (`TenantSetting`) when allowed.
152: 4. Organization-scoped options when delegated by tenant.
153: 
154: Every admin control must surface:
155: 
156: - Effective value.
157: - Source of value.
158: - Lock reason if not editable.
159: 
160: ## Authorization Model
161: 
162: Introduce explicit policies:
163: 
164: - `InstanceAdminPolicy`
165: - `TenantAdminPolicy`
166: - `OrganizationAdminPolicy`
167: 
168: Use policy + claims + membership checks where required; reduce direct role-string checks in UI and handlers.
169: 
170: ## Single-Tenant Behavior
171: 
172: In `SingleTenant` mode:
173: 
174: - UI may merge instance+tenant experiences for usability.
175: - Backend still enforces scope semantics.
176: - Multi-tenant-only endpoints/features are hidden or blocked.
177: 
178: In `MultiTenant` mode:
179: 
180: - Scope separation is explicit in menu, routes, and endpoint access.
181:

581: 
582: ## Risk Assessment and Mitigations
583: 
584: | Risk | Severity | Mitigation |
585: |---|---|---|
586: | Role/claim mismatch between IdP and API policies | High | Define mapping contract + integration tests early in Phase 4/6. |
587: | Static tenant header causes cross-tenant defects | Critical | Complete Task 4.3 before enabling tenant admin release. |
588: | Runtime mode switching introduces inconsistent behavior | High | Resolve mode via settings + cache invalidation + rollback flow. |
589: | Lock bypass via direct API call | High | Enforce lock checks in handlers, not only UI. |
590: | Manual route list drift in Blazor | Medium | Centralize route definitions + add route coverage tests. |
591: | Migration conflicts in active branches | Medium | Isolate migration updates and verify idempotent scripts. |
592: 
593: ## Success Metrics
594: 
595: ### Security/Correctness
596: 
597: - 100 percent admin endpoint policy coverage in integration tests.
598: - Zero tenant isolation violations in test matrix.
599: - Zero lock bypass defects in governance command tests.
600: 
601: ### Product Behavior
602: 
603: - Runtime deployment mode change effective on next request.
604: - Tenant admins can configure submission/verification policies within delegated boundaries.
605: - Organization admins can operate only in their organization scope.
606: 
607: ### Maintainability
608: 
609: - No Clean Architecture boundary violations introduced.
610: - Shared reusable admin components for lock/source UX.
611: - Setting key catalog is explicit and documented.
612: 
613: ## Required Resources and Dependencies
614: 
615: ### Technical Dependencies
616: 
617: - IdP role mapping updates for `InstanceAdmin`, `TenantAdmin`, `OrganizationAdmin`.
618: - EF migration execution window and rollback verification.
619: - OpenAPI/NSwag refresh process for new admin endpoints.
620: 
621: ### Team Dependencies
622: 
623: - Product owner decision on delegation of tenant onboarding controls.
624: - Security review for policy model.
625: - QA support for role matrix and runtime mode switch regression scenarios.
626: 
627: ## Effort Estimate
628: 
629: | Phase | Effort | Duration (approx) |
630: |---|---|---|
631: | Phase 0 | M | 3-4 days |
632: | Phase 1 | M | 4-6 days |
633: | Phase 2 | XL | 8-12 days |
634: | Phase 3 | L | 6-9 days |
635: | Phase 4 | L | 5-8 days |
636: | Phase 5 | XL | 10-15 days |
637: | Phase 6 | L | 6-9 days |
638: 
639: Total estimated range: 42-63 engineering days (single engineer equivalent), excluding external approvals.
640: 
641: ## Exit Criteria (Definition of Done)
642: 
643: - [ ] All phase acceptance criteria completed.
644: - [ ] API + Blazor scope/role test matrix green.
645: - [ ] Migrations verified in dev/staging with rollback path.
646: - [ ] Docs and operational runbooks updated.
647: - [ ] Admin pages are role-separated, lock-aware, and functional in single and multi-tenant modes.

172: 
173: The `EventApiClient.g.cs` is auto-generated. Changes to this file will be overwritten.

187: **Action**: Verify enums exist in NSwag client or create manual copies in Phase 6
188: 
189: ### BFF Pattern
190: 
191: Blazor communicates with API through BFF (Backend-for-Frontend):
192: - `BffClient.cs` handles token forwarding
193: - `BrowserCredentialsMessageHandler.cs` adds credentials
194: - YARP proxies `/api/*` to actual API

## File: dev/active/blazor-api-sync/blazor-api-sync-plan.md
````markdown
  1: # Blazor-API Synchronization - Implementation Plan
  2: 
  3: > **Comprehensive refactor to bring Blazor frontend in sync with API capabilities**
  4: >
  5: > Created: 2026-01-31
  6: 
  7: ## Executive Summary
  8: 
  9: The API has significantly evolved with HATEOAS support, Event Aspects (Islamic/Tech), enhanced DTOs, and new federation features. The Blazor frontend currently uses hardcoded routes and lacks UI for Event Aspects entirely. This plan addresses the gap by:
 10: 
 11: 1. Implementing a HATEOAS-aware service layer for hypermedia-driven navigation
 12: 2. Creating Event Aspects UI components (Islamic and Tech)
 13: 3. Synchronizing all domain entities between API and Blazor
 14: 4. Maintaining existing patterns (MudBlazor, BEM, BFF architecture)
 15: 
 16: **Estimated Effort**: 3-4 development sessions
 17: **Risk Level**: Medium (non-breaking changes, additive functionality)
 18: 
 19: ---
 20: 
 21: ## Current State Analysis
 22: 
 23: ### API Capabilities (Available)
 24: 
 25: | Feature | Status | Notes |
 26: |---------|--------|-------|
 27: | HATEOAS Links | Implemented | 28+ link policies, HAL format responses |
 28: | Event Aspects | Implemented | Islamic and Tech aspects with full CQRS |
 29: | Pagination | Implemented | PagedResponse with metadata |
 30: | Federation (ATProto) | Implemented | PDS sync outbox, IndexedDid |
 31: | Multi-tenancy | Implemented | Virtual tenant masking |
 32: | Module System | Partial | ModuleDefinition entity exists |
 33: 
 34: ### Blazor Capabilities (Current)
 35: 
 36: | Feature | Status | Gap |
 37: |---------|--------|-----|
 38: | HATEOAS Consumption | Missing | Hardcoded routes in services |
 39: | Event Aspects UI | Missing | No components, no services |
 40: | Pagination UI | Partial | Uses PagedResponse but no MudTable virtualization |
 41: | Federation UI | Missing | No ATProto management UI |
 42: | Multi-tenancy UI | Missing | No tenant switching UI |
 43: 
 44: ### Critical Gaps Identified
 45: 
 46: 1. **HATEOAS Not Consumed**: EventService uses `_apiClient.EventGET2Async(eventId)` with hardcoded method names instead of following `_links`
 47: 2. **Event Aspects Missing**: EventDto includes `IslamicAspect` and `TechAspect` but Blazor ignores them
 48: 3. **NSwag Client Ignores Links**: Generated client returns DTOs but discards HATEOAS metadata
 49: 4. **No Link-Based Navigation**: Blazor uses `Href="/events"` instead of following API links
 50: 
 51: ---
 52: 
 53: ## Proposed Architecture
 54: 
 55: ### HATEOAS Consumption Strategy
 56: 
 57: **Option A: Link-Aware Service Wrapper** (Recommended)
 58: ```
 59: EventService -> HateoasClient -> NSwag Client -> API
 60:                     |
 61:                     v
 62:               Link Resolution
 63: ```
 64: 
 65: **Option B: Custom HTTP Client with Link Parsing**
 66: ```
 67: EventService -> HateoasHttpClient -> API
 68:                     |
 69:                     v
 70:               Parse _links from response
 71: ```
 72: 
 73: **Decision**: Option A - Wrap existing NSwag client to preserve type safety while adding link awareness.
 74: 
 75: ### Component Architecture for Event Aspects
 76: 
 77: ```
 78: EventDetail.razor
 79:     |
 80:     +-- EventIslamicAspectCard.razor (conditional)
 81:     |       |
 82:     |       +-- IslamicAspectEditDialog.razor
 83:     |
 84:     +-- EventTechAspectCard.razor (conditional)
 85:             |
 86:             +-- TechAspectEditDialog.razor
 87: ```
 88: 
 89: ---
 90: 
 91: ## Implementation Phases
 92: 
 93: ### Phase 1: HATEOAS Foundation (Priority: High)
 94: 
 95: **Goal**: Create infrastructure for consuming HATEOAS links from API responses
 96: 
 97: #### Task 1.1: Create HateoasLink Model
 98: - **File**: `Explore.Blazor.Client/Models/HateoasLink.cs`
 99: - **Purpose**: Represent `_links` from API responses
100: - **Acceptance**: Model can deserialize HAL-format links
101: 
102: #### Task 1.2: Create IHateoasClient Interface
103: - **File**: `Explore.Blazor.Client/Services/Contracts/IHateoasClient.cs`
104: - **Purpose**: Define contract for link-aware API calls
105: - **Methods**:
106:   - `Task<T?> FollowLinkAsync<T>(HateoasLink link)`
107:   - `Task<T?> GetWithLinksAsync<T>(string url)` where T : IHasLinks
108:   - `Task<TResult?> ExecuteActionAsync<TResult>(HateoasLink link, object? payload)`
109: - **Acceptance**: Interface compiles, follows SOLID principles
110: 
111: #### Task 1.3: Implement HateoasClient
112: - **File**: `Explore.Blazor.Client/Services/HateoasClient.cs`
113: - **Purpose**: HTTP client that parses and follows HATEOAS links
114: - **Dependencies**: BffClient (existing), JsonSerializer
115: - **Acceptance**: Can GET a resource and extract its `_links`
116: 
117: #### Task 1.4: Create IHasLinks Interface
118: - **File**: `Explore.Blazor.Client/Models/IHasLinks.cs`
119: - **Purpose**: Mark DTOs that have HATEOAS links
120: - **Acceptance**: EventDto, OrganizationDto implement interface

312: 
313: ## Risk Assessment
314: 
315: | Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
316: |------|------------|--------|------------|
317: | NSwag client regeneration breaks changes | Medium | High | Document which files are generated vs manual |
318: | HATEOAS parsing breaks on API changes | Low | Medium | Version API, use schema validation |
319: | Performance impact from extra HTTP calls | Low | Low | Cache links, batch requests where possible |
320: | Existing tests fail | Medium | Medium | Run tests before and after each phase |
321: 
322: ---
323: 
324: ## Success Metrics
325: 
326: 1. **Event Aspects Display**: EventDetail shows Islamic/Tech aspects when present
327: 2. **Aspect CRUD Works**: Can create, update, delete aspects from UI
328: 3. **HATEOAS Foundation**: At least EventService uses link-based navigation
329: 4. **No Regressions**: All existing functionality continues to work
330: 5. **Tests Pass**: Unit and integration tests green
331: 
332: ---
333: 
334: ## Dependencies
335: 
336: - **API must be running**: All Blazor development depends on API endpoints
337: - **NSwag regeneration**: May need to regenerate client after API changes
338: - **MudBlazor version**: Ensure compatible with current project
339: 
340: ---
341: 
342: ## Timeline Estimate
343: 
344: | Phase | Estimated Time |
345: |-------|---------------|
346: | Phase 1: HATEOAS Foundation | 2-3 hours |
347: | Phase 2: Event Aspects Service | 1-2 hours |
348: | Phase 3: Event Aspects UI | 3-4 hours |
349: | Phase 4: Create Flow Integration | 1-2 hours |
350: | Phase 5: HATEOAS Navigation | 2-3 hours |
351: | Phase 6: Lookup Sync | 1 hour |
352: | Phase 7: Styling | 1-2 hours |
353: | **Total** | **11-17 hours** |
354:

## File: dev/active/blazor-pagination-support/blazor-pagination-support-plan.md
````markdown
  1: # Blazor Pagination Support - Implementation Plan
  2: 
  3: **Last Updated**: 2026-01-15
  4: 
  5: ## Executive Summary
  6: 
  7: The API now returns paginated results for GetAll endpoints, while Blazor (Explore.Blazor and Explore.Blazor.Client) still expects full lists and performs in-memory paging and filtering. This plan updates the generated API client, service layer, and list-based UI components to consume paginated responses consistently, with server-driven pagination and updated UX for totals and page navigation.
  8: 
  9: ## Current State Analysis
 10: 
 11: - API controllers (example: `Explore.API/Controllers/EventController.cs`) return `PaginatedResult<T>` with `pageNumber` and `pageSize` query parameters.
 12: - Blazor client services return `ICollection<T>` from `*AllAsync()` endpoints and load entire lists (example: `Explore.Blazor.Client/Services/EventService.cs`).
 13: - UI components apply local pagination and filtering on full lists (example: `Explore.Blazor.Client/Pages/Event/EventList.razor`, `Explore.Blazor.Client/Pages/Event/MyEvents.razor`).
 14: - NSwag-generated client (`Explore.Blazor.Client/Clients/EventApiClient.g.cs`) is outdated and does not model paginated responses.
 15: 
 16: ## Proposed Future State
 17: 
 18: - API client supports paginated endpoints and exposes `PaginatedResult` models (generated or wrapped).
 19: - Service interfaces accept pagination parameters and return paginated results.
 20: - List pages (events, orgs, registrations, admin tables) request pages explicitly and display counts based on API metadata.
 21: - Lookup tables continue to load fully using `pageSize = 100` or multi-page fetch helpers.
 22: 
 23: ## Implementation Phases (Clean Architecture Alignment)
 24: 
 25: ### Phase 1: Contract and Client Alignment (API Client Layer)
 26: 
 27: **1.1 Regenerate or Update API Client for Pagination**
 28: - Files: `Explore.Blazor.Client/Clients/EventApiClient.g.cs` (generated)
 29: - Update client to include query parameters and paginated response types for all GetAll endpoints.
 30: - Acceptance Criteria:
 31:   - `EventAllAsync` and other `*AllAsync` methods include `pageNumber` and `pageSize` parameters (optional or overloads).
 32:   - Paginated response models are generated (e.g., `PaginatedResultOfEventListDto`) or a custom wrapper exists.
 33: - Effort: M
 34: - Dependencies: API Swagger schema reflects paginated responses
 35: - Related Skills: `blazor-bff-patterns`
 36: 
 37: **1.2 Define a Shared Pagination Model (if needed)**
 38: - Files: `Explore.Blazor.Client/Models/PaginatedResult.cs` (new, if not generated)
 39: - Acceptance Criteria:
 40:   - Single generic model with `Items`, `PageNumber`, `PageSize`, `TotalCount`, `TotalPages`, `HasPreviousPage`, `HasNextPage`.
 41: - Effort: S
 42: - Dependencies: 1.1
 43: - Related Skills: `clean-architecture-rules`
 44: 
 45: ### Phase 2: Blazor Client Service Updates (Application Layer in UI)
 46: 
 47: **2.1 Update Core Services to Return Paginated Results**
 48: - Files: `Explore.Blazor.Client/Services/EventService.cs`, `Explore.Blazor.Client/Services/EventService.Operations.cs`, `Explore.Blazor.Client/Services/LandingPageService.cs`
 49: - Change `GetAllEventsAsync` and `GetMyEventsAsync` to accept `pageNumber` and `pageSize` and return paginated results.
 50: - Acceptance Criteria:
 51:   - Service methods return paginated results without breaking error handling.
 52:   - Landing page queries use pageSize limits and read totals from metadata.
 53: - Effort: M
 54: - Dependencies: 1.1, 1.2
 55: - Related Skills: `cqrs-mediatr-guidelines`
 56: 
 57: **2.2 Update Lookup and Admin Services for Pagination**
 58: - Files: `Explore.Blazor.Client/Services/CategoryService.cs`, `Explore.Blazor.Client/Services/TagService.cs`, `Explore.Blazor.Client/Services/LocationService.cs`, `Explore.Blazor.Client/Services/AdminService.cs`, `Explore.Blazor.Client/Services/EventRegistrationService.cs`, `Explore.Blazor.Client/Services/OrganizationService.cs`, `Explore.Blazor.Client/Services/OrganizationMemberService.cs`, `Explore.Blazor.Client/Services/OrganizationReviewService.cs`
 59: - Acceptance Criteria:
 60:   - Add paged methods or update existing list methods to accept pagination parameters.
 61:   - Lookup helpers fetch all pages when needed (pageSize=100, loop while `HasNextPage`).
 62: - Effort: L
 63: - Dependencies: 1.1, 1.2
 64: - Related Skills: `blazor-bff-patterns`
 65: 
 66: ### Phase 3: UI Component Refactors (Presentation Layer)
 67: 
 68: **3.1 Event List Page (Public Explore)**
 69: - File: `Explore.Blazor.Client/Pages/Event/EventList.razor`
 70: - Replace local `AllFilteredEvents` paging with server-driven pagination.
 71: - Update filter behaviors to request new pages; re-evaluate category/tag filter endpoints for pagination support.
 72: - Acceptance Criteria:
 73:   - Page navigation updates the API request `pageNumber`.
 74:   - Results count uses API `TotalCount` and `TotalPages`.
 75:   - Filters reset pagination to page 1 and request a new page.
 76: - Effort: L
 77: - Dependencies: 2.1
 78: - Related Skills: `blazor-ui-conventions`
 79: 
 80: **3.2 My Events Page**
 81: - File: `Explore.Blazor.Client/Pages/Event/MyEvents.razor`
 82: - Replace local pagination with paginated `GetMyEventsAsync` calls.
 83: - Acceptance Criteria:
 84:   - My events list reflects API pagination and totals.
 85:   - Page controls are enabled/disabled based on API metadata.
 86: - Effort: M
 87: - Dependencies: 2.1
 88: - Related Skills: `blazor-ui-conventions`
 89: 
 90: **3.3 Admin and Management Lists**
 91: - Files: `Explore.Blazor.Client/Pages/Admin/AdminList.razor`, `Explore.Blazor.Client/Pages/Admin/Tags.razor`, `Explore.Blazor.Client/Pages/Admin/Categories.razor`, `Explore.Blazor.Client/Pages/Admin/Locations.razor`, `Explore.Blazor.Client/Pages/Organization/OrganizationMembers.razor`, `Explore.Blazor.Client/Pages/User/MyRegistrations.razor`
 92: - Update list pages to use paginated service calls and show totals.
 93: - Acceptance Criteria:
 94:   - Each list page requests pages explicitly and displays pagination controls.
 95:   - All counts reflect API `TotalCount`.
 96: - Effort: L
 97: - Dependencies: 2.2
 98: - Related Skills: `blazor-ui-conventions`
 99: 
100: **3.4 Shared Pagination Component (Optional)**
101: - Files: `Explore.Blazor.Client/Components/Common/PaginationControls.razor` (new)
102: - Acceptance Criteria:
103:   - Shared component supports MudPagination and emits page changes.
104:   - Used by multiple pages for consistent UI.
105: - Effort: S
106: - Dependencies: 3.1
107: - Related Skills: `blazor-ui-conventions`
108: 
109: ### Phase 4: BFF/Server Integration Check (Explore.Blazor)
110: 
111: **4.1 Validate BFF Proxy Expectations**
112: - Files: `Explore.Blazor/Extensions/BFF_REFACTORING_README.md`, any BFF endpoint mappings
113: - Acceptance Criteria:
114:   - No hardcoded assumptions about non-paginated responses in server-side proxying.
115:   - Documentation updated if BFF endpoints now expect pagination parameters.
116: - Effort: S
117: - Dependencies: 1.1
118: - Related Skills: `blazor-bff-patterns`
119: 
120: ### Phase 5: Testing and Validation
121: 
122: **5.1 Manual UI Validation**
123: - Verify Event List, My Events, Admin lists, and registrations paging.
124: - Acceptance Criteria:
125:   - Pagination controls switch pages without errors.
126:   - Totals display correctly for all updated pages.
127: - Effort: M
128: - Dependencies: 3.1, 3.2, 3.3
129: 
130: **5.2 Build Verification**
131: - Run `dotnet build Explore.sln` and resolve compile issues if any.
132: - Acceptance Criteria:
133:   - Build succeeds without errors.
134: - Effort: S
135: - Dependencies: All prior phases
136: 
137: ## Detailed Tasks with Acceptance Criteria
138: 
139: 1. Update NSwag client to include paginated responses and page parameters.
140:    - Acceptance: Generated methods return paginated models and include `pageNumber`, `pageSize`.
141:    - Effort: M
142: 
143: 2. Update EventService and LandingPageService to use paginated responses.
144:    - Acceptance: Event list and landing page data use API pagination metadata.
145:    - Effort: M
146: 
147: 3. Update lookup/admin services to support pagination or multi-page fetch.
148:    - Acceptance: All list-fetch methods handle paginated responses.
149:    - Effort: L
150: 
151: 4. Refactor `Explore.Blazor.Client/Pages/Event/EventList.razor` and `Explore.Blazor.Client/Pages/Event/MyEvents.razor` to server pagination.
152:    - Acceptance: UI uses API totals and fetches pages on demand.
153:    - Effort: L
154: 
155: 5. Refactor admin and management list pages to server pagination.
156:    - Acceptance: Each page loads via paged service calls with UI pagination.
157:    - Effort: L
158: 
159: 6. Validate UI manually and fix any edge cases.
160:    - Acceptance: Pagination works across all updated screens.
161:    - Effort: M
162: 
163: ## Risk Assessment and Mitigation
164: 
165: - Risk: API does not support pagination for some filter endpoints (category/tag/session lists).
166:   - Mitigation: Confirm API endpoints; if missing, keep limited fetch (pageSize=100) or add API changes in follow-up.
167: - Risk: NSwag client regen changes DTO names and breaks references.
168:   - Mitigation: Isolate changes to generated file and update service interfaces accordingly.
169: - Risk: UX regressions in filtering when data no longer loaded locally.
170:   - Mitigation: Reset page on filter change and validate counts with API metadata.
171: 
172: ## Success Metrics
173: 
174: - All Blazor list pages load with paginated API responses and no full-table fetches.
175: - UI pagination shows accurate totals and page counts.
176: - `Explore.Blazor.Client/Pages/Event/EventList.razor` and `Explore.Blazor.Client/Pages/Event/MyEvents.razor` no longer rely on in-memory pagination over full datasets.
177: 
178: ## Required Resources and Dependencies
179: 
180: - Updated API Swagger with paginated response schemas.
181: - NSwag client generation workflow (see prior NSwag refactor notes if needed).
182: - MudBlazor pagination component usage.
183: 
184: ## Effort Estimates
185: 
186: - Phase 1: 0.5-1 day
187: - Phase 2: 1-2 days
188: - Phase 3: 2-3 days
189: - Phase 4: 0.5 day
190: - Phase 5: 0.5-1 day
191: 
192: Total Estimate: 4-7 days
````

## File: dev/active/blazor-refactoring/blazor-refactoring-plan.md
````markdown
  1: # Plan: Blazor Project Comprehensive Refactoring
  2: 
  3: **Last Updated: 2026-02-06**
  4: 
  5: ---
  6: 
  7: ## Executive Summary
  8: 
  9: The Explore Blazor projects (`Explore.Blazor` and `Explore.Blazor.Client`) contain **2 CRITICAL security vulnerabilities, 12 HIGH severity issues, 16 MEDIUM severity issues, and 10+ LOW severity issues** across security, architecture, code quality, dead code, and test coverage. The overall test coverage is approximately **9%** (7 test files covering ~81 testable units). This plan addresses all findings systematically across 8 phases, ordered by risk and impact.
 10: 
 11: ### Key Findings Summary
 12: 
 13: | Category | Critical | High | Medium | Low |
 14: |----------|----------|------|--------|-----|
 15: | Security Vulnerabilities | 2 | 5 | 4 | 1 |
 16: | Dead/Unused Code | 0 | 3 | 4 | 3 |
 17: | Architecture Violations | 0 | 2 | 4 | 2 |
 18: | Code Quality & Standards | 0 | 4 | 6 | 4 |
 19: | Test Coverage Gaps | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 |
 20: | Performance Issues | 0 | 0 | 3 | 0 |
 21: | **Total** | **2** | **15** | **21** | **10** |
 22: 
 23: ### Current State vs Future State
 24: 
 25: | Aspect | Current State | Future State |
 26: |--------|--------------|--------------|
 27: | Security | Auth debug endpoints public; cross-user token leakage; CSP disabled | All debug endpoints removed/guarded; scoped token service; CSP enabled |
 28: | Render Mode | InteractiveServer (contradicts docs saying InteractiveAuto) | InteractiveAuto with proper WASM support or cleaned-up Server-only |
 29: | Token Handling | Static ConcurrentDictionary; GetAnyValidToken cross-user risk | Scoped service per-user; no cross-user fallback |
 30: | Test Coverage | ~9% (7 files / ~101 tests) | >60% (~300+ tests across services, pages, components) |
 31: | Code Standards | 50+ files missing ABOUTME; 30+ Console.WriteLine; Dutch/English mix | All files compliant; structured logging; English only |
 32: | Dead Code | 6+ unused files; 3 excluded-from-compilation files | All dead code removed |
 33: | CancellationToken | Zero usage in Blazor Client services | All async methods accept CancellationToken |
 34: | Code Duplication | GetInitials (4x), GetEventColor (4x), image upload (3x) | Shared helpers/base classes; single source of truth |
 35: | Authorization | Missing [Authorize] on EventEdit, CreateOrganization, etc. | All write pages properly guarded |
 36: | Validation | DataAnnotationsValidator used; FluentValidation validators exist but unused | FluentValidation wired throughout; server+client validation |
 37: 
 38: ---
 39: 
 40: ## Phase 1: Critical Security Fixes (Week 1)
 41: 
 42: **Priority**: CRITICAL / BLOCKING
 43: **Effort**: M
 44: **Related Skills**: `auth-patterns`, `blazor-bff-patterns`
 45: 
 46: ### Task 1.1: Remove/Guard Auth Debug Endpoints
 47: 
 48: - **File**: `Explore.Blazor/Program.cs`, lines 606-667
 49: - **Acceptance Criteria**:
 50:   - [ ] `/auth/debug` endpoint removed entirely from production code
 51:   - [ ] `/auth/status` returns only `{ isAuthenticated: bool, name: string }` for authenticated users; nothing for unauthenticated
 52:   - [ ] No Keycloak authority, client ID, client secret, or discovery document exposed in any endpoint
 53:   - [ ] Error responses in auth challenge (lines 564-577) return generic message only; details logged server-side
 54:   - [ ] Sign-out error handler (line 601) follows same pattern
 55: - **Effort**: S
 56: - **Dependencies**: None
 57: 
 58: ### Task 1.2: Fix Cross-User Token Leakage in CircuitAccessTokenService
 59: 
 60: - **File**: `Explore.Blazor/Services/CircuitAccessTokenService.cs`, lines 24-28, 133-158
 61: - **Acceptance Criteria**:
 62:   - [ ] Remove `static ConcurrentDictionary<string, TokenEntry>` shared state
 63:   - [ ] Remove `static _latestToken` fallback
 64:   - [ ] Remove `GetAnyValidToken()` method entirely
 65:   - [ ] Simplify to a scoped service with per-circuit `_accessToken` property matching documented pattern in `blazor-bff-patterns/resources/token-forwarding.md`
 66:   - [ ] If token not found for current circuit, return null (not another user's token)
 67:   - [ ] `AccessTokenForwardingHandler` receives token from scoped `ICircuitAccessTokenService`
 68:   - [ ] All token-related `Console.WriteLine` replaced with `ILogger` at Debug level
 69: - **Effort**: M

 73:

 75: - **Acceptance Criteria**:
 76:   - [ ] Auth cookie `SecurePolicy` set to `CookieSecurePolicy.Always` in production, `SameAsRequest` in development only
 77:   - [ ] XSRF-TOKEN cookie has explicit `Path = "/"`
 78:   - [ ] XSRF-TOKEN cookie `Secure` flag is `true` in production (not `ctx.Request.IsHttps`)
 79:   - [ ] Forwarded headers (lines 374-381) have documented known-network restriction or explicit comment about trusted-proxy-only deployment
 80: - **Effort**: S
 81: - **Dependencies**: None

 84: 
 85: - **File**: `Explore.Blazor/Components/App.razor`, lines 14-20
 86: - **Acceptance Criteria**:

 88:   - [ ] `script-src` restricts to `'self'` and `_content/MudBlazor/` path
